name: Race Broadcast
author: Apoc
description: Watch AI races like TV: the AI drives your car, the race goes on after a crash, an auto director follows the action, with replays and a four-voice commentary team.

options.label: AI drive: on/off key
options.description: Press in a race to let the game's AI drive your car; press again to take over.

options.label: AI drive: from the start
options.description: The AI takes your car a few seconds after the race starts (races only).

options.label: AI drive: take-over countdown
options.description: When you take the car back: at once, or after a countdown.

options.label: Broadcast: on/off key
options.description: Turns the broadcast camera on or off by hand.

options.label: Broadcast: start when the AI drives
options.description: Switches to the broadcast as soon as the AI has your car.

options.label: Broadcast: start when your car is out
options.description: Watch the rest of the race after you crash or retire.

options.label: Crash: keep the race running
options.description: When your car is wrecked the race goes on and you watch it (idea and method from Spectator/Broadcast Mode by Kizi & RK).

options.label: Crash: send the wreck to the garage
options.description: Seconds after the crash, or never.

options.label: Director: auto camera
options.description: The camera follows the best story: incidents, overtakes, battles, the leader.

options.label: Director: on/off key
options.description: Turns the auto director on or off during the broadcast (off = use the game's own keys).

options.label: Director: minimum shot length (s)
options.description: How long the camera stays on a car before it may move to a better battle. Incidents cut in sooner.

options.label: Director: camera
options.description: Broadcast camera, TV pod (onboard), or a mix (onboard for battles, broadcast for the rest).

options.label: Director: favour my car
options.description: Show your own car more often.

options.label: Replays (experimental)
options.description: Auto director only. Offers replays of contact, the start, restarts and big overtakes (F9 to watch), or plays them automatically. Works through the pause menu: keep the game window in front.

options.label: Commentary (optional, beta)
options.description: On (Normal) by default. Ben (lead), Graham (expert), Tom (pit lane) and Erin (strategy), with a preview on the formation lap. Voices: see Commentary voices. Restart the game after changing.

options.label: Commentary voices
options.description: Recorded: natural voices recorded with Google Gemini, with drivers' names (no download). Piper: free offline voices that read every detail live (about 250 MB download on first use).

options.label: Graphics: use Project Aeternum
options.description: While Project Aeternum is running, it draws the broadcast graphics: our captions and tower stand down, the game's spectator HUD is not held up, and telemetry is read on Aeternum's port 20778.

options.label: Graphics: director runs Aeternum
options.description: The director decides which of Project Aeternum's graphics are on screen: battle for, catching, driver cards, pit lane, tyres, damage, weather. The leaderboard stays as your profile has it; the track map is kept off.

options.label: Graphics: director places Aeternum's graphics
options.description: Places the car graphics (live speed, tyre life, car status, pit lane, weather...) in the bottom right corner, stacking upwards. The leaderboard stays where your Aeternum layout puts it.

options.label: Graphics: captions
options.description: A lower-third caption saying why the camera is on that car.

options.label: Graphics: own timing tower
options.description: Our own tower on the left. Off by default: the addon keeps the game's spectator timing tower up instead.

options.label: Graphics: game notifications too
options.description: Also show each story in the game's own race notification.

options.label: Event feed (for testing)
options.description: Writes every story to addon-storage\apoc.race-broadcast\events.txt. Not needed for the commentary.

options.label: Keys: game's camera key
options.description: Pressed once when the broadcast ends, so your normal camera comes back. Set it to your change-camera key.

options.label: Telemetry: UDP port
options.description: The port the game's UDP telemetry is sent to (Settings > Telemetry: UDP On, IP 127.0.0.1, format 2026 or 2025). Use 20778 if another program already uses 20777.

options.label: Debug log
options.description: Logs every story the director sees.
